key_insight: Post-selection and entanglement are distinct resources: post-selection can boost CHSH weak values, but only entanglement lets those correlations exceed the separable PPS bound.
engineering_relevance: The work suggests hybrid weak-measurement protocols that can act as entanglement witnesses and may improve sensing or state characterization beyond standard Bell tests.
method: Analyze anomalous weak values of the CHSH operator in pre- and post-selected ensembles.
Compare three bound cases: unrestricted boundary states, one separable boundary state, and both boundary states separable.
Optimize over Bell operators and state overlap to derive maximal weak values and generalized PPS bounds.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical optimization results showing that the enhancement beyond separable bounds tracks concurrence, and that a constructive protocol can detect every pure two-qubit source state with nonzero concurrence in the ideal state-adapted setting.
watch_item: The strongest guarantees rely on ideal, state-adapted post-selection and measurement choices, so practical performance may be limited by alignment errors, noise, and imperfect post-selection efficiency.
paper_title: Quantum nonlocal correlations of anomalous weak values
